title: Hard but lightweight ‘bio-metal’ material discovered in sea worm jaws | New Scientist
description: Marine bristle worms have jaws made from a mix of proteins and metal ions that may constitute a whole new kind of material, with possible applications in engineering
author: Karmela Padavic-Callaghan

title: Why praying for rain appears to work – but only in some places | New Scientist
description: In some parts of the world, the probability of rain rises with every day it doesn’t rain, and communities in these places are more likely to carry out rain-making rituals
author: Bas den Hond

title: The US-China AI arms race has taken an unexpected turn | New Scientist
description: Powerful artificial intelligence models built by Chinese companies have gone from inducing widespread panic to being met with a shrug of the shoulders – what changed?
author: Matthew Sparkes

title: Maya mathematician's name decoded alongside astronomical formula | New Scientist
description: Hieroglyphs on the wall of a Maya building record calculations concerning the orbits of Earth, Mars and Venus, as well as the name of a mathematician who wrote the text around 1200 years ago
author: James Woodford

title: Sugar molecules found in interstellar space for the first time | New Scientist
description: Researchers have long suspected early life may have been helped by sugars brought to Earth by asteroids – now a sugar found in raspberries has been spotted in a cosmic cloud nearly 27 light years away
author: Christa Lesté-Lasserre

title: Shifts in the jet stream are behind Europe's long heatwaves | New Scientist
description: Two types of jet stream patterns seem to be causing persistent heat domes over Europe, with big questions for the future
author: Alec Luhn
